paragraph: Single-family is the North Arlington market, with 36 sales over six months at a median of $638,500. This is a real seller's market: 78 percent of homes sold above asking, the sale-to-list ratio is 1.05, and the median days on market is 14.5 with the fastest sale at seven days. Prices ran from $460,000 to $1,155,000, so the median is the better guide than either end. Multi-family is the second tier, 12 sales at a median of $820,000, a 1.02 ratio, half selling above asking, and a median of 19.5 days on market. Two, three, and four-family houses here draw both owner-occupants who want a unit to rent and straight investors, and that competition is why the multi-family median sits well above the single-family one. Monthly counts are thin, mostly under 10 closings, so no single month proves much, but the run from April through July held between $610,000 and $675,000 rather than sliding. If the usual seasonal arc holds, expect closings and medians to ease as fall sets in. If you're weighing tiers, the question is space and grounds for yourself or a second unit paying part of the mortgage.
